title: Augmented strict reduction tower of ordinary pullback
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. Use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, small pro-etale sites, coefficient sheaves $B_W=A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$, and strict tower categories of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], for $W=T,T'$. Put $R_W=\underline A_W$, $S_{n,W}=\underline{P_n}_W=(P_n)_W$, and write $\operatorname{Res}_W:D(B_W)\to D(R_W)$ for exact restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use the canonical finite coefficient comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and the derived module pullbacks of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

For any $K\in D(B_T)$, without a completeness hypothesis, put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{n,T}$ and $N=Lg^*_{R}\operatorname{Res}_T K$. Let $H_\bullet=Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$, a complex of strict $B_{T'}$-towers whose finite coefficient evaluations are $H_n=Lg_n^*K_n$. Let $\mathcal R(N)_n=N\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$ denote the strict reduction tower computed on one flat-term K-flat representative [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum, def-pc-kflat-complex].

There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\tau:\mathcal R(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{T'}H_\bullet$ in the derived category of strict $R_{T'}$-towers, induced by an isomorphism of strict diagrams on compatible K-flat models. Its finite coefficient evaluation is the composite $\tau_n$ of the canonical pullback/tensor comparison with $Lg_n^*$ of the finite constant-to-completed scalar comparison. It commutes with every quotient transition and carries the quotient augmentation from the constant tower on $N$ to the restriction of the pulled-back quotient augmentation, precomposed with the ordinary constant-to-completed pullback comparison.

For $\widehat N=R\lim\mathcal R(N)$, using total right derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], it induces an isomorphism $\rho:\operatorname{Res}_{T'}(R\lim H_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat N$. If $p_n^H,p_n$ are the respective evaluations, then $\operatorname{Res}(p_n^H)=\tau_n p_n\rho$. Under $\rho$ the pulled-back augmentation gives the quotient-completion unit $\eta:N\to\widehat N$, and $p_n\eta=u_n$, the finite scalar-extension unit. All comparisons are natural in $K$.

proof.text: Write $U=g^{-1}$, $R=R_T$, $B=B_T$, $R'=R_{T'}$, $D=B_{T'}$, $C=UB$, $S_n=S_{n,T}$, and $S_n'=S_{n,T'}$. The flatness and quotient assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] give $R\to B$, $R'\to D$ flat, with $B\otimes_RS_n=S_n$ and $D\otimes_{R'}S_n'=S_n'$. The constant-sheaf identifications and exactness of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identify $UR=R'$ and $US_n=S_n'$. Choose a flat-term K-flat $B$-representative $P$ of $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements] for the one-object category. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat], $\operatorname{Res}P$ is flat-term K-flat over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], $M=U\operatorname{Res}P$ is such a representative of $N$ over $R'$, and $Q=UP$ is flat-term K-flat over $C$ (use the transported-ring structural isomorphism $UB=C$). Inverse image here is exact on underlying abelian sheaves, so computes the constant-coefficient derived pullback without boundedness.

Put $F_n=P\otimes_BS_n$, with transition $1\otimes q_{b,a}$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] this strict diagram represents $K_\bullet$. The augmented strict comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-common-quotient-reduction-tower] identifies $\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_RS_n$ with $\operatorname{Res}F_n$. Applying the cochain tensor comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] to constant-coefficient pullback, and then inverse image of this comparison, gives strict isomorphisms
$$c_n:M\otimes_{R'}S_n'\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}'(UF_n).$$
Write $T_n=UF_n$, with its $S_n'$-action and induced $D$-action. Exact finite coefficient pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] shows that $T_n$ represents $Lg_n^*K_n$. These complexes are K-flat over $S_n'$, by the normalization calculation in the adic datum and preservation of K-flatness under finite pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. No assertion that $T_n$ is K-flat over $D$ or $R'$ is needed.

proof.text: To identify this entire augmented diagram with the derived tower pullback, let $J$ be the small category with objects $*$ and positive integers, arrows $*\to n$ and $b\to a$ for $b\geq a$, with the evident composition. Let $A_J$ be the $R$-diagram $R[0]\to S_n[0]$. Choose one strict objectwise flat-term K-flat replacement $V_J\to A_J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements]. The augmented $B$-diagram $E_j=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RV_j)$ maps to $P$ at $*$ and to $F_n$ at $n$, using the strict common-quotient comparison in step 2. These are quasi-isomorphisms because $\operatorname{Res}P$ is K-flat. Every $E_j$ is flat-term K-flat over $B$: write it as $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B(B\otimes_RV_j))$, apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] to $V_j$, and [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] to this tensor. Thus $E_J$ is a resolving-class replacement of the whole augmented reduction diagram, not unrelated choices at its levels.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); the small augmented-diagram application is the argument of this step.

proof.text:
Put $V_j'=UV_j$, so its augmentations to $A_j'=R'[0]$ for $j=*$ and $A_j'=S_j'[0]$ otherwise are quasi-isomorphisms. Pulling $E_J$ back over $B\to D$ gives the strict diagram
$$Z_j=\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_C(D\otimes_{R'}V_j')),$$
by the ordinary tensor and scalar balancing maps [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Flatness of $D$ over $R'$ and its common quotients from [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] make $D\otimes_{R'}V_j'\to D\otimes_{R'}A_j'$ quasi-isomorphisms, with targets $D$ at $*$ and $S_n'$ at $n$. Since $Q$ is K-flat over $C$, tensoring these maps with $Q$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Hence there is one strict objectwise quasi-isomorphism of augmented diagrams from $Z_J$ to the diagram with source $Q\otimes_CD=g_B^*P$, levels $Q\otimes_CS_n'=T_n$, and quotient augmentation. The finite identification is inverse image of the ordinary balancing map defining $F_n$; exactness of $U$ is [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. This proves that $T_\bullet$ is a compatible representative of $H_\bullet=Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$ by [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. In particular no flatness of $C\to D$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); sites-modules.tex Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat). The quasi-isomorphism test is the K-flat definition applied to the cone.

proof.text: The maps $c_n$ in step 2 are therefore an isomorphism of strict representatives of $\mathcal R(N)$ and $\operatorname{Res}'H_\bullet$; let $\tau$ be its localization. On the sheafified pure tensors of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], $c_n$ sends $x\otimes s$ to the corresponding $x\otimes s$. Both transition composites send $x\otimes s$ to $x\otimes q_{b,a}(s)$. The source map $M\to\operatorname{Res}'(Q\otimes_CD)$ is scalar insertion $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Following it by the pulled-back quotient augmentation sends $x$ to $x\otimes1$ in $T_n$, as does $c_n$ after the quotient augmentation $M\to M\otimes_{R'}S_n'$. These are equalities of maps of strict complexes, including the augmented source. The tensor comparison and common-quotient comparison used in step 2 are exactly the two factors specified for $\tau_n$ in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback): pure tensor formulas; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, proof; quotient and scalar-insertion units as in steps 2–4.

proof.text: For a chain map between flat-term K-flat representatives $P\to\widetilde P$, every displayed comparison commutes with it: on pure tensors both orders give $f(x)\otimes s$, and all maps in $Z_J\to T_J$ are induced by coefficient augmentations. By [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements], pullback carries quasi-isomorphisms of resolving diagrams to quasi-isomorphisms; finite reduction has this property by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The universal resolving-class construction [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], applied also to the augmented indexing category $J$, therefore descends these comparisons and equalities to the derived functors, independently of the representatives. This proves the asserted canonicity and naturality of $\tau$ as an augmented tower comparison, rather than only a collection of isomorphisms after evaluation.

proof.text:
Restriction along $R'\to D$ is exact since it leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Its left adjoint is scalar extension [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction], which is exact by the flatness of $D$ in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. These adjunctions act levelwise on strict towers, and exactness there is levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] says that restriction preserves K-injective tower complexes. Take a K-injective tower resolution $T_\bullet\to J_\bullet$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; its restriction is a K-injective resolution of $\operatorname{Res}'T_\bullet$. Inverse limit commutes with restriction literally: both are the sheaf of compatible families with its $R'$-action. Hence the same complex $\operatorname{Res}'\lim J_n=\lim\operatorname{Res}'J_n$ gives a canonical isomorphism
$$\lambda:\operatorname{Res}'(R\lim H_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim\operatorname{Res}'H_\bullet.$$
It respects evaluations since both evaluation maps are the same projections $\lim\operatorname{Res}'J_n\to\operatorname{Res}'J_n$. This computation does not replace derived products with underived ones.

source.place: Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0940 (section-derived-limits), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); sites-modules.tex Tags 03D7 and 03DA for the scalar adjunction.

proof.text:
Using the total right derived limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], define
$$\rho=(R\lim\tau)^{-1}\lambda:\operatorname{Res}'(R\lim H_\bullet)\longrightarrow R\lim\mathcal R(N)=\widehat N.$$
It is invertible because both factors are. Naturality of evaluation gives $p_n^{\operatorname{Res}H}(R\lim\tau)=\tau_np_n$; this is also the equality obtained by taking the $n$th component of the same map between K-injective tower resolutions. Step 7 identifies $p_n^{\operatorname{Res}H}\lambda$ with $\operatorname{Res}'p_n^H$. Composing with $\rho$ gives precisely $\operatorname{Res}'p_n^H=\tau_np_n\rho$.

source.place: Tags 0940 (section-derived-limits), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok): evaluation from a K-injective strict tower resolution.

proof.text: The quotient-completion unit for $M$ is obtained from its strict compatible maps $M\to M\otimes_{R'}S_n'$ by composing with a tower K-injective resolution and factoring through the termwise limit. The pulled-back augmentation is constructed in exactly this way in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. By the strict augmented equality of step 5, precomposing it with scalar insertion gives those same quotient maps after $\tau_n$. The resolution comparison defining $R\lim\tau$ and the common restricted resolution defining $\lambda$ therefore identify the two factorization maps: after $\rho$ the pulled-back augmentation is $\eta:N\to\widehat N$. Projecting this factorization to its $n$th component gives $p_n\eta=u_n$, not merely equality up to an unspecified choice of cone map. Steps 6–8 and the functorial total right derived limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] make $\lambda,\rho,\eta$ and these identities natural in $K$. No completeness assumption on $K$ has entered any step.

split_report.summary: Retained the statement and all imported metadata; supplied a nine-step proof using only existing nodes. The whole augmented coefficient diagram is resolved at once to identify the derived tower pullback, finite reductions use one flat-term K-flat representative, restriction preserves tower K-injectives by its exact left adjoint, and evaluations and completion units are computed on these models. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes paragraph 2 of the current completed-pullback-reduction proof: pull back the strict reduction tower and identify it with the reduction tower of ordinary constant-coefficient pullback, before finite reduction of completion. Also makes the augmentation and derived-limit evaluation normalization explicit. No chapter or unit route is changed.

tool_uses.why: Exact constant-coefficient inverse image and its ring identification on a geometric morphism are generic tools; no proper-base-change-unit statement supplies the assertion for the possibly infinite ring A.

The explicit chain-level tensor and scalar-association isomorphisms are needed before localization to keep the strict quotient diagram and its augmentation; the unit’s bifunctorial derived tensor statement alone does not supply chain formulas.
Generic scalar extension preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms; used for B tensor_R V_j, not as a replacement of the unit route.
Generic total tensor closure and reassociation for unbounded flat-term K-flat complexes are used to put E_J in the diagram resolving class.
The universal resolving-class construction descends the actual natural chain maps and augmented equalities; it is a generic derived-functor tool.
The ordinary extension/restriction adjunction supplies the exact left adjoint needed for K-injective preservation on towers.

Step 1: flat-term K-flat P; Res P stays K-flat because the completed ring is flat over the constant one; pullback preserves K-flat with no flatness of c needed. Step 2: the common-quotient node gives a strict tower iso including the cone; tensor coherence gives c_n; exact finite pullback gives T_n = Lg_n^*K_n. Step 3: the augmented category J (objects * and n≥1) is resolved strictly. This is needed because F_n is not K-flat over B. The E_j are flat-term K-flat by change-of-rings and the total-tensor-model node. Step 4: I checked by hand that g^*E_j ≅ Tot(Q⊗_C(D⊗_{R'}V'_j)). Flatness of D over R' and K-flatness of Q over C give quasi-isomorphisms onto (g^*P, T_•), because UB→D→S_n' equals U(B→S_n). Step 5: the pure-tensor identities for transitions and augmentation hold, and the source map is the scalar-extension comparison of constant-completion-equivalence. Step 6: descent through roofs via the resolving-class node. Step 7: Res' has an exact left adjoint (by flatness), so 08BJ applies levelwise on towers and lim commutes with restriction literally. Step 8: the type check gives Res'p_n^H = τ_n p_n ρ. Step 9: η comes from the units computed on the shared restricted resolution, and p_nη = u_n. Edge cases K=0, g=id, I=0 and unbounded K are all fine. The six declared tool_uses are generic tools and accepted; right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective is in sk-def-exchange, which the unit cites, so it is on the route. No SGA is cited.
